utility.notes: Georgia Power (a Southern Company subsidiary) is the well-established dominant electric utility for the Augusta area — not independently cross-checked against a dedicated Georgia Power service-territory map this session.

value.name: Georgia Power
value.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Augusta's residential solar customers this session; Georgia Power is recorded as both the distribution and default generation utility.

county.notes: Augusta and Richmond County operate a consolidated city-county government; the License and Inspection Department is the single permitting authority for the entire consolidated jurisdiction.

permit_authority.value: Augusta-Richmond County License and Inspection Department
permit_authority.notes: Georgia has no single statewide permitting agency — each of Georgia's 159 counties and its municipalities administers its own building department under the state's minimum standard codes (adopted IRC/IBC/NEC with Georgia Amendments). Augusta-Richmond County's consolidated government gives it a single permitting authority for the whole jurisdiction, similar in structure to Durham, NC and Sumter, SC's consolidated city-county departments researched earlier this session.

interconnection_url.notes: See the identical Georgia Power interconnection program notes on the Atlanta record (ga-fulton-atlanta-georgiapower) — Georgia Power does not offer retail-rate net metering; residential customers choose between 'RNR Instantaneous Netting' (up to 250kW AC, Solar Avoided Energy Cost Rate credit, $100 interconnection fee) or 'Energy Offset' (no size limit, no grid compensation, default enrollment).

value.name: Two sets of plans covering mounting and electrical work
Structural evaluation report from an engineer confirming the roof can support the solar panels and associated equipment

required_documents.notes: Per the Department's own FAQ page confirming a permit is required for solar panel installation. Commercial installations require three sets of plans prepared by a licensed engineer (not applicable to this residential record).

value: Inspections are requested online through the Department's own Inspection Request form

timeline_days.notes: No specific review-to-issuance day count was published on the Department's permit information page this session.

other_conditions: Per the Department's general residential permitting page, single-family permits are issued to licensed contractors, or to the homeowner directly only if the homeowner will own and occupy the house

value.name: Electrical permit
value.notes: Per the Department's own Permit Fees page — this is the general residential electrical permit fee, applicable to a solar installation's electrical work; not a dedicated solar line item.

value.name: Building permit
value.notes: Per the Department's own Permit Fees page — this is the general residential building permit formula based on the house's square footage under roof, not a dedicated solar valuation-based fee.

permit_fees.notes: Both figures are the Department's general residential permit fee schedule (not solar-specific line items); the Permit Fees page itself notes it contains no dedicated information on solar panel installations.

rebates.notes: Per Georgia Power's own statement (see interconnection_url notes on the Atlanta record), neither Georgia Power nor the State of Georgia currently offers incentives or rebates for residential solar — recorded as null/no-program rather than unresearched.
